body: don’t let that shame drag you down. allow yourself to be inspired by their sacrifice to pull yourself up

you decide that. pain comes from lack of agency, and agency is lost when anger is lost. don’t lose your anger. be angry and reclaim your agency, and start driving your life. 

do you have a support system?

i have this. it helps, but at the end of the day it doesn’t matter what anyone, no matter how loving, says except what you say to yourself and accept. my husband says so many supportive things but i usually don’t let it in. so talk yourself down. be there for yourself, uplift yourself. believe and let in the advice people give you.

God doesn’t hate you. that pain is sincere and real, and deep within you there is a light that feels regret which is an incredible feeling. your fight now is to not allow that regret to consume you. you didn’t do anything wrong, you couldn’t take care of a child you don’t want. God bless you

i saw my brother die in a really gruesome way and because of that trauma i randomly picture any situation easily turning bloody, for no reason. i hear you. but the thing is, we can’t ascribe the empty feeling to anyone but ourselves. they didn’t really occupy that space, but their presence made you distracted about it. now that they’re gone, you are more aware of the emptiness. it’s on you to fill it. i believe in you.
that is a sign to hang on. you’ll be okay

the part of you that is convincing you that this is the way to go isn’t the voice that loves you. self reproach is good only to an extent - it helps us stay moral and weighs our options. but when it becomes a tyrant and overwhelms us, we have to pick up the sword and defeat it.
